facts.statement: Timimus lived during the Early Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Early Cretaceous

facts.statement: Timimus was a small theropod dinosaur that lived in Australia during the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Timimus is a genus of small coelurosaurian theropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of Australia.

facts.statement: Two femurs, one from an adult and one from a juvenile, were discovered within one meter of each other at the Dinosaur Cove East site in southern Australia in 1991.
facts.quote: In 1991, two femora (thighbones), one from an adult and one from a juvenile, were found within a metre of each other at the Dinosaur Cove East site, in the small "Lake Copco" quarry, at the southern tip of Australia.

facts.statement: Timimus hermani was formally named and described by Dr. Thomas Rich and Patricia Vickers-Rich in 1993 or 1994.
facts.quote: The type species, Timimus hermani, was formally named and shortly described by Dr Thomas Rich and his wife Patricia Vickers-Rich in 1993/1994.

facts.statement: The genus name Timimus means 'Tim's Mimic', combining the names of the discoverers' son Timothy Rich and paleontologist Tim Flannery.
facts.quote: The generic name means "Tim's Mimic" and combines the name of both the discoverers' son Timothy Rich and palaeontologist Tim Flannery with a Latin mimus, "mimic", a reference to the presumed affinity of the species with the Ornithomimosauria.

facts.statement: The species name hermani honors the volunteer John Herman who assisted the Dinosaur Cove project.
facts.quote: The specific name honours volunteer John Herman who, for many years, assisted the Dinosaur Cove project.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen dates to the Albian stage of the Early Cretaceous, approximately 106 million years ago.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, NMV P186303, was found in a layer of the Eumeralla Formation, dating to the Albian faunal stage in the early Cretaceous, some 106 million years ago.

facts.statement: The holotype femur measures 44 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: The holotype thighbone is 44 centimetres long.

facts.statement: Based on the femur length, the total estimated length of the animal is 2.5 meters.
facts.quote: From this, a total length of the animal of 2.5 metres has been extrapolated.

facts.statement: The slender femur suggests that Timimus was a lithe animal.
facts.quote: The slenderness of the bone suggest a lithe animal.

facts.statement: A 2016 estimate suggests the holotype specimen was 4.3 meters long and weighed 200 kilograms.
facts.quote: In 2016 the NMV P186303 specimen was estimated to be 4.3 meters (14 ft) long, and 200 kg (441 lbs) in weight.

facts.statement: Timimus was originally classified as an ornithomimosaur but is now thought to be a tyrannosauroid.
facts.quote: It was originally identified as an ornithomimosaur, but now it is thought to be a different kind of theropod, possibly a tyrannosauroid.

facts.statement: It is now recognized that Timimus lacks shared derived traits with ornithomimosaurs, providing no proof of its membership in that group.
facts.quote: Today, it is recognised that Timimus shares no derived traits, synapomorphies, with the Ornithomimosauria and thus any proof it would belong to this group is lacking.

facts.statement: A 2010 study classified Timimus within Paraves, possibly as an indeterminate dromaeosaurid related to Unenlagiinae.
facts.quote: A 2010 study classified Timimus within Paraves, specifically as Dromaeosauridae? indet. cf. Unenlagiinae.

facts.statement: A 2012 study identified Timimus as a valid tyrannosauroid, a view supported by later analyses that placed it either within Tyrannosauroidea or as a sister taxon to Tyrannoraptora.
facts.quote: A 2012 study found it to be a valid tyrannosauroid, a conclusion supported by Delcourt and Grillo (2018) who recovered Timimus as a tyrannosauroid in two phylogenetic analyses but as a sister taxon of Tyrannoraptora (outside Tyrannosauroidea) in one analysis.

facts.statement: Timimus lived in polar forests with mild summers and cold, dark winters due to the region's proximity to the South Pole in the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: The habitat of Timimus consisted of polar forests with mild summers but cold and dark winters due to the closer proximity of the area to the South Pole during the Early Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Analysis of bone microstructure suggests Timimus may have hibernated during colder months, unlike the ornithischian Leaellynasaura.
facts.quote: The ornithischian showed a continuous rate of bone deposition, while the coelurosaur had a cyclical pattern of bone formation, which suggested Timimus may have hibernated in colder months.

facts.statement: A fossilized toe bone from a possible Timimus relative shows a depressed fracture on the bottom surface, suggesting injury.
facts.quote: A possible Timimus hermani or related form from the Strzelecki Group near Inverloch, Victoria left a fossil of the first phalanx of its third toe with a depressed fracture on the plantar surface.

facts.statement: Timimus was found in the Otway Group at Dinosaur Cove in Victoria, Australia.
facts.quote: Fue encontrado en el grupo Otway, de la Ensenada del Dinosaurio, en Victoria (Australia).

facts.statement: Timimus was initially classified as an ornithomimosaur but is now believed to be a tyrannosauroid or an unenlagiine.
facts.quote: Inicialmente fue clasificado como un ornitomimosauriano, pero actualmente se cree que es un tipo diferente de terópodo, un tiranosauroide o un unenlagiino.

facts.statement: In 2016, the holotype specimen was estimated to be 4.3 meters long and weigh 200 kilograms.
facts.quote: En 2016, se estimó que la muestra NMV P186303 tenía 4,3 metros de largo y 200 kilogramos de peso.

facts.statement: Cyclical bone growth patterns in Timimus suggest it hibernated during the cold nights of the Early Cretaceous, unlike the active Leaellynasaura.
facts.quote: En la ultraestructura de los huesos de Timimus se ve un crecimiento en forma cíclica, lo que podría indicar que este dinosaurio hibernaba, en las frías noches australianas del Cretácico Inferior a diferencia de Leaellynasaura, que permanecía activo en la larga noche polar.

facts.statement: Two femurs, one from an adult and one from a juvenile, were found less than a meter apart at the Dinosaur Cove East site in southern Australia in 1991.
facts.quote: En 1991, se encontraron dos fémures, huesos del muslo, uno de un adulto y otro de un juvenil, a menos de un metro uno del otro en el sitio Dinosaur Cove East, en la pequeña cantera "Lake Copco", en el extremo sur de Australia.

facts.statement: The species Timimus hermani was formally named and briefly described by Dr. Thomas Rich and his wife Patricia Vickers-Rich between 1993 and 1994.
facts.quote: La especie tipo, Timimus hermani, fue nombrada formalmente y descrita brevemente por el Dr. Thomas Rich y su esposa Patricia Vickers-Rich entre 1993 y 1994.

facts.statement: The genus name means "Tim's imitator" and combines the names of the discoverers' son, Timothy Rich, and paleontologist Tim Flannery with the Latin word for "mimic," referencing the supposed affinity with ornithomimosaurs.
facts.quote: El nombre del género significa "El imitador de Tim" y combina el nombre del hijo de los descubridores, Timothy Rich, y del paleontólogo Tim Flannery con un latín mimus , "mimico", una referencia a la supuesta afinidad de la especie con los ornitomimosaurianos.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, NMV P186303, was found in the Eumeralla Formation and dates to the Albian stage of the Early Cretaceous, approximately 106 million years ago.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo , NMV P186303, se encontró en una capa de la Formación Eumeralla , que data de la etapa faunística del Albiense a principios del Cretácico, hace unos 106 millones de años.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a left femur from an adult individual.
facts.quote: Consiste en un fémur izquierdo de un individuo adulto.

facts.statement: The second femur, from a juvenile, was designated as the paratype specimen NMV P186323.
facts.quote: El segundo fémur, el de un juvenil, fue asignado como paratipo , espécimen NMV P186323.

facts.statement: Timimus was initially classified as a basal ornithomimosaurian based on femur characteristics.
facts.quote: Timimus ha sido clasificado como un ornitomimosauriano basal, debido a las características de los fémures.

facts.statement: Recent studies have proposed that Timimus does not provide conclusive evidence of being an ornithomimosaurian and should be reclassified.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, recientes estudios han propuesto que Timimus no provee de evidencia conclusiva que haya sido un ornitomimosauriano y que debe ser reclasificado.

facts.statement: It is now recognized that Timimus does not share derived traits with Ornithomimosauria, lacking proof of its membership in that group.
facts.quote: Hoy en día, se reconoce que Timimus no comparte rasgos derivados, sinapomorfias, con el Ornithomimosauria y, por lo tanto, falta cualquier prueba de que pertenecería a este grupo.

facts.statement: A 2012 study found Timimus to be a valid tyrannosauroid, a conclusion supported by Delcourt and Grillo in 2018.
facts.quote: Un estudio de 2012 encontró que era un tiranosauroide válido, una conclusión respaldada por Delcourt y Grillo en 2018.

facts.statement: Timimus lived in polar forests with mild summers but cold, dark winters due to the area's proximity to the South Pole during the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: El hábitat de Timimus consistía en bosques polares con veranos suaves pero inviernos fríos y oscuros debido a la mayor proximidad del área al Polo Sur durante el Cretácico Inferior.

facts.statement: Analysis of bone histology suggested Timimus may have hibernated during colder months, indicated by a cyclic bone formation pattern compared to continuous growth in ornithischians.
facts.quote: El ornitisquio mostró una tasa continua de deposición ósea, mientras que el celurosaurio tuvo un patrón cíclico de formación ósea, lo que sugirió que Timimus pudo haber hibernado en los meses más fríos.

facts.statement: A fossil of the first phalanx of the third toe with a depressed fracture on the plantar surface was found, possibly belonging to Timimus hermani or a related form from the Strzelecki Group near Inverloch, Victoria.
facts.quote: Un posible que Timimus hermani o forma relacionada del Grupo Strzelecki cerca de Inverloch, Victoria dejó un fósil de la primera falange de su tercer dedo del pie con una fractura deprimida en la superficie plantar.

facts.statement: Timimus lived from the Albian to the Cenomanian stages, between 113.2 and 93.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Cenomanian (113.2 to 93.9 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The head of the femur is flattened from front to back.
rejected.quote: The femoral head is anteroposteriorly flattened.
